An episode of transient loss of consciousness with no clear etiology identified on initial evaluation. The patient experienced a sudden, unwitnessed loss of consciousness with no prodrome, no injury, and no post-ictal features (e.g., confusion, fatigue, or focal neurological deficits — though not explicitly assessed, absence of tongue biting/incontinence makes seizure less likely). gaps.info: Detailed witnessed description of event (duration, motor activity, responsiveness, recovery pattern)
gaps.discriminates: Arrhythmic syncope vs. psychogenic pseudosyncope vs. epilepsy — e.g., prolonged unresponsiveness with normal vitals favors PNES; brief tonic-clonic movements with rapid recovery favor arrhythmic syncope; postictal confusion favors epilepsy
